'''''Viburnum odoratissimum''''', the '''sweet viburnum''', is a shrub or small tree in the family [[Viburnaceae]]. It is native to Asia, and commonly cultivated as a garden ornamental elsewhere.

==Description==
[[File:Folhas jovens de viburno-perfumado (Viburnum odoratissimum) em Bagé, RS, Brasil - 55231754354.jpg|thumb|left|Young leaves growing from the bottom of the trunk, in Brazil]]
[[File:Viburnum odoratissimum var. awabuki kz01.jpg|thumb|left|Flowers]]
It grows to 9 metres high and has dull elliptical leaves to 20 cm long. In spring it produces pyramid-shaped clusters of fragrant white flowers, followed by red berries that age to black.<ref name="LordWillis1982">{{cite book |author1=Lord, Ernest Edward |author2=Willis, James Hamlyn |title=Shrubs and Trees for Australian Gardens |year=1982 |publisher=Lothian }}</ref>

==Distribution and habitat==
The species is native to China, Korea, Taiwan, Japan, the Himalayan region in India, Myanmar, Thailand, Vietnam and the Philippines.<ref name=GRIN>{{GRIN |access-date=9 April 2014 }}</ref>

''Viburnum odoratissimum'' var. ''awabuki'', now considered by some authorities to be its own species, ''[[Viburnum awabuki]]'', and with glossy leaves, is native to Korea ([[Jeju Island]]), Taiwan, and Japan.<ref name="GRIN awabuki">{{GRIN |''Viburnum odoratissimum'' var. ''awabuki'' |310737 |access-date=9 April 2014 }}</ref>

==Cultivation==
The species prefers warm, frost-free climates.<ref name="LordWillis1982"/>{{Dubious|reason=The plant is native to places that get frost in the winter, particularly the Himalayas, Korea and Japan, which have cool winters even in their warmest areas (such as Jeju Island). I suspect a falsified source.|date=November 2022}}
